51587373.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to his-tagged human PD-L1 assessed as dissociation constant by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Binding Affinity: The binding affinity of compounds with human PD-L1/B7-H1 Protein, His Tag, ACRO, PD1-H5229) and the mouse PD-L1 IgV domain (Mouse PD-L1/B7-H1 Protein, His Tag, ACRO, PD1-M5220) was assessed using a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare Biosciences, Sweden). In brief, PD-L1 or PD-1 was diluted in sodium acetate solution (pH 4.5) to a final concentration of 50 μg/mL and immobilized onto a CMS chip, following a standard amine-coupling procedure. Compounds were serially diluted using a PBS buffer containing 0.05% Tween 20 and 5% DMSO to appropriate concentrations and then injected over the chip following a predefined program. The Kd value was determined using Biacore T200 evaluation software (GE Healthcare).
original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Crystallization: The DNA encoding human PD-L1 (18–134) with a C-terminal 6His tag was inserted into the pET21b vector and transformed into BL21 (DE3) cells for protein expression. The purified inclusion bodies were dissolved in a solution containing 50 mM Tris HCl (pH 8.0), 200 mM NaCl, and 8 M urea and then refolded by diluting with a solution of 50 mM Tris HCl (pH 8.0), 0.5 M arginine, 2 mM reduced-GSH, and 0.2 mM oxidized-GSH with a gradient of urea concentrations from 6 to 0 M. The refolded protein was purified using a Superdex S75 column equilibrated. The hPD-L1 protein at a concentration of 2.5 mg/mL was mixed with compound X18 at a molar ratio of 1:3 and incubated on ice for 60 min. The resulting protein complex was screened for crystallization at 16 °C using a 1:1 ratio of protein to reservoir solution, following the sitting-drop vapor-diffusion method. Diffraction-quality crystals of hPD-L1/X18 complex were obtained from 19% PEG3350% and 0.2 M ammonium tartrate dibasic. The crystals were cryoprotected by the reservoir solution with 25% MPD and flash-frozen in liquid nitrogen for the diffraction data collection. The diffraction data of the crystals were collected at 100 K at the beamlines BL18U1 at Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facility and were processed using the HKL3000 software packages. The structures were solved via molecular replacement with the CCP4 program, utilizing a search model from PDB code 5C3T. The model was built using Coot, and subsequent refinement was performed using PHENIX. Data collection and refinement statistics are provided in Table S1.
original_paragraph.Results and Discussion - Binding Affinit: The binding affinity of X3, X7, X18, and L7 was determined by the surface plasmon resonance (SPR) method. The results of SPR kinetic analysis shown in Table 4 confirmed that all these compounds have strong binding affinity with PD-L1. In order to further assess the interspecies selectivity of X18, we employed SPR to evaluate the binding affinity of X18 with murine PD-L1 (mPD-L1). The results demonstrated that X18 also exhibited high affinity for mPD-L1, with a dissociation constant (Kd) of 31.8 nM (Figure S1).
